objective: Normalized Drell-Yan q_T shape from two Gaussian TMD PDFs (synthetic widths)

observable.process: Drell-Yan h1 h2 -> l+ l- X: normalized q_T shape (1/sigma) d sigma/d^2q_T

normalization.convention: normalized to unit integral over d^2q_T

conventions.unit_system: natural-HEP: transverse momenta in GeV, Gaussian widths <k_perp^2>, <p_perp^2>, M'^2 in GeV^2; F_UU,T and the q_T shape per GeV^2; asymmetries dimensionless
conventions.frame: SIDIS: gamma* - nucleon frame (Trento conventions): virtual photon along +z, nucleon P = P0(1, 0, 0, -1), incoming lepton l = E(1, sin theta, 0, cos theta) with a positive x component, lepton plane = x-z plane (Anselmino et al. p. 2); any frame reached from the target rest frame by a boost along q-hat; Drell-Yan: hadronic centre-of-mass frame for q_T
conventions.angle_definition: phi_h, phi_S: azimuths of P_hT and S_T about the photon axis, measured from the lepton plane; phi: azimuth of the quark k_perp
conventions.azimuth_convention: Trento conventions (Trento Eq. 16; Bacchetta et al. Eq. 2.3) for phi_h and phi_S. Anselmino et al. use the same angles: with l_x > 0, P_T = P_T(cos phi_h, sin phi_h, 0) and S_T = |S_T|(cos phi_S, sin phi_S, 0) (pp. 2, 6, 11), Trento Eq. 16 gives cos phi_h and sin phi_h unchanged (mapping in derivations/derivation-record.md, step 5)
conventions.exchanged_bosons: photon only (one-photon exchange in SIDIS; virtual photon in Drell-Yan)
conventions.mass_approximation: massless partons; target and hadron masses neglected (gamma = 2Mx/Q -> 0 in Bacchetta et al. Eqs. 2.8-2.11)
conventions.tmdg:gaussian_ansatz: f_q(x, k) = f_q(x) exp(-k^2/<k_perp^2>)/(pi <k_perp^2>), D_q(z, p) = D_q(z) exp(-p^2/<p_perp^2>)/(pi <p_perp^2>), p = hadron transverse momentum relative to the fragmenting quark, P_hT = z k + p at O(k/Q) (Anselmino et al. Eqs. 29, 34-35); constant, flavour-independent widths
conventions.tmdg:fragmentation_normalization: Anselmino: int d^2p D(z, p) = D(z) (Eq. 37). Bacchetta: D_1(z) = z^2 int d^2k_T D_1(z, k_T^2), k_T the quark relative to the hadron, hadron relative to quark = -z k_T (Eq. 3.41), so <p_perp^2> = z^2 <k_T^2>

allowed_transformations: multiply by the LO collinear cross section for an absolute q_T spectrum
never compare with data: widths are synthetic
